name: Shoreham
intro: Shoreham is a small Western Port settlement where narrow roads run down to a quiet foreshore and inland to vineyards. Shoreham Beach and Honeysuckle Beach change with the tide: tidal flats appear at low water, while deeper swimming water is available around mid to high tide. There is no surf lifesaving patrol at Shoreham Beach, so check conditions and supervise children near the water. Ocean Eight is a local winery on Tucks Road; confirm current tasting access with the operator before travelling. Come for the coast and the slower pace, with a few planned stops rather than a full-service village.
factualLede: Shoreham is a Western Port coastal village with two beaches, tidal flats at low tide and no surf lifesaving patrol at Shoreham Beach.

tldr: Shoreham is a small Western Port coast stop with tidal beaches and rural wine-country roads nearby.
Best for: quiet foreshore walks and visitors who want a slower coastal stop.
Signature experience: a shore walk after checking the tide, then a winery visit confirmed with its operator.
Allow half a day, with supplies packed before you arrive.
notFor: anyone wanting lots of dining options
signature: A tiny coastal settlement where bush, vineyard and beach sit almost on top of each other.
skip: Turning up expecting a full-service village - Shoreham is a beach and a few roads, nothing more.
bestDay: Pack what you need, walk the Shoreham foreshore after checking the tide, then visit a winery only after confirming its current access.
insiderNote: Shoreham Beach is unpatrolled. Check tides and conditions before entering the water and supervise children closely.
